title: 📰 AI news · October 29

items.title: AI agents got into Anthropic's internal systems through third-party tools
items.text: The startup Cathedral was hunting for bugs under Anthropic's own bounty program. Its AI agents got in through third-party sales and admin software and found meeting records and salary data. Claude chats and code were not affected. If you run a bot or agent, external services are connected around it too. Check which services are linked to your agent and what rights they have.

items.title: An Anthropic model built working exploits for Chrome, Safari, Windows and Linux
items.text: In a lab, an unreleased model chained the flaws it found into working attacks. Anthropic gave Google 62 Chrome bugs, and all reported flaws are patched. If you haven't updated your browser and system in a while, they stay open. Update your browser and system today. Free guide "Protecting your computer, code and access": send the word "protect" to the bot.

items.title: GMO offers $1 million for the hackers behind a trader cloud breach
items.text: A service used by FX traders was breached and about $50 million was demanded. The company refused to pay. Customers saw trades they never made. If you trade or keep money through a remote service, change your password and turn on two-factor protection.

items.title: Sony's internet provider leaked data of 2.58 million people
items.text: Names, phones, emails and birth dates leaked, plus 54,401 email passwords. No banking data was involved. If you reuse one password, a leak in one service opens the others. Check whether your email password repeats elsewhere.

items.title: Discord will open public server messages to search engines
items.text: From November 16, public servers with 1,000+ members get open web pages, and from mid-December messages can appear in search. If you run a Discord community, your discussions become visible to everyone. Decide in advance which channels to close.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon
items.text: The model for long engineering tasks arrived two weeks after Argon. It scored 59 on the Artificial Analysis index versus 50 and took first place. Price is unchanged, access is limited to selected specialists for now.

items.title: Android Studio now plugs in more than 40 AI coding agents
items.text: They include Claude Agent and Codex. Google's tests show interface tasks finishing 77% faster.

items.title: Chrome autofill can now search your Gmail
items.text: Chrome will fill forms with flight, order and address details found in your emails. It starts in the US and you turn it on yourself in settings.

items.title: Apple shows the first Mac with a touchscreen
items.text: The new MacBook Pro with a two-layer OLED starts at $2,899. Dynamic Island replaces the camera notch. Sales begin November 6.

items.title: Google will allow one-tap installs from third-party Android stores
items.text: Stores vetted by Google get one-tap installs. Starts December 1, and the US is not among the countries.

items.title: iQOO Neo12 arrives with a built-in fan and a 9,000 mAh battery
items.text: A 59-blade fan cools the phone during games. The screen runs at 185 Hz, charging is 100 W, and the price in China is about $630.

items.title: XREAL shows wired smart glasses on Android XR
items.text: The glasses weigh under 95 grams and show up to five apps. Price is $1,099, shipping from mid-November.

takeaway: Today's news is about what attackers go through: third-party tools, reused passwords, outdated browsers. Recommendation: list the external services connected to your bot and accounts and check their rights.
